stories.title: Polling under way for NA-77, PP-203 by-elections in Punjab
summary: Rashid and 17 other candidates have filed nomination papers to contest the constituency, but opposition parties, including the PTI, PPP and Jamaat-i-Islami (JI), have not opted for the by-election.
This is the second time that the by-election is being held in the constituency after the 2024 general elections.
Subsequently, the ECP scheduled a by-election for Nov 23, 2025, which was won by Jutt with 46,820 votes.

stories.title: Usman Khawaja denies throwing 'anyone under the bus' with comments about Australia's 2018 ball-tampering scandal
summary: Usman Khawaja insisted on Sunday he did not “throw anyone under the bus” by claiming the entire Australian team was in on the 2018 “Sandpapergate” plot and defended taking eight years to go public.

That probe found only Smith, Warner and Bancroft were in the know. “When I mentioned it was all of us, that’s implying that whether we like it or not, we’re all responsible for what happened together as a team,” Khawaja said in a lengthy Instagram post on Sunday.

That’s the first time I tried to come out.” Khawaja said he again almost spoke up in 2021 when bowlers Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon all denied publicly that they knew about the ball-tampering.

stories.title: Bomb Disposal Squad official martyred as IED goes off in KP's South Waziristan
summary: SOUTH WAZIRISTAN: An assistant head of the police’s Bomb Disposal Squad (BDS) was martyred after an improvised explosive device (IED) went off in the Janta area of Sararogha tehsil in Upper South Waziristan district on Saturday while he was attempting to defuse it.

Upper South Waziristan district police officer (DPO) Ashfaq Khan told Dawn that the official, identified as Abdul Jabbar, was busy defusing the IED when an explosion occurred, leaving him seriously injured.

On the same day, an incident was reported in Toi Khulla Bazaar in Lower South Waziristan district, where an unidentified person wearing a burqa threw a hand grenade near the place where police personnel were seated.

stories.title: PTI's Gohar demands end to ‘political victimisation’
summary: SWAT: Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Saturday called for judicial independence, rule of law and an end to what he described as political victimisation.
The PTI chairman said that access to party founder Imran Khan, including meetings with his personal physician and family members, remained their foremost demand.
Describing political isolation and what he termed “political apartheid” as harmful to democracy, Barrister Khan expressed concern over the alleged illegal detention of political leaders.

stories.title: Pak-Afghan trade cannot proceed amid terrorism: Samar Haroon Bilour
summary: She said the reopening of trade routes depended on addressing Pakistan’s legitimate security concerns and securing practical cooperation from the Afghan authorities.

She urged Kabul to ensure that its territory was not used by militant groups to carry out attacks against Pakistan. “The threat of terrorism persists, but the law and order situation in the province has improved,” the governor’s adviser said in a statement issued by her office.
The governor’s adviser also confirmed that Pakistan’s national flag had been hoisted on government buildings and offices in the areas concerned.

stories.title: Governor invites Chinese investors to explore KP’s potential
summary: The meeting, attended by a delegation of Chinese investors, focused on investment opportunities in the province, particularly in the minerals sector, as well as the potential for investment in its economic zones, according to a statement issued by the governor’s office.

He said the province faced enormous challenges, including terrorism, displacement and prolonged instability, which had placed additional pressure on the healthcare system and other essential public services, according to another statement issued by the governor’s office.

The governor said people deserved a healthcare system that served them with dignity, empathy and responsibility and that professional organisations such as the Pakistan Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons could play a significant role in improving healthcare services.

stories.title: Joint investigation team formed to probe violent clashes after court hearing in Sindh's Kotri
summary: Another person, Azeem Barejo, who was injured during the scuffle, was taken to the Liaquat University Hospital, Jamshoro, by his brother, Dhani Bakhsh, who had proceeded to the court after hearing about the scuffle.
The FIR was lodged against Dhani Bakhsh, his son Sarmad and brothers, Azeem, Aslam, Sharif and Ismail.
The court hearing on Friday pertained to an application for confirmation or otherwise of a pre-arrest bail filed by Azeem, his brother Sharif and their nephew Sarmad (son of Dhani Bakhsh).

stories.title: Karachi SHO suspended after audio of apology to drug dealer surfaces
summary: KARACHI: The station house officer (SHO) of the Pak Colony police station was suspended after an audio clip went viral on social media in which he purportedly sought an apology from a drug dealer.

According to an order, an audio recording surfaced on social media on Nov 5, allegedly featuring the SHO and a police constable in an “unauthorised, compromising conversation with a known drug peddler, Kashif alias Dada”.
The SHO had “compromised the writ of law” by pursuing mutual reconciliation with a criminal and directing his subordinate to apologise to the drug peddler, the order stated.

stories.title: Islamabad's Capital Development Authority plans to challenge court order over Bari Imam House
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Capital Development Authority has decided to challenge the Islamabad High Court’s interim order that directed it to de-seal Bari Imam House.
The IHC had on November 3 directed the CDA and other respondents to “forthwith de-seal the premises” and barred any further demolition until the next hearing.

The CDA, which sealed the premises on October 30 in a joint operation with the district administration, claimed the structure stands on government land and was among properties identified for action under its anti-encroachment drive.

stories.title: ‘No suitable candidate’ among nearly 100 applicants for Pakistan Council of Scientific and Industrial Research's top post
summary: Under Section 4(1)(a) read with Section 5(1) of the PCSIR Act, 1973, the ministry has proposed that Dr Abidi be re-nominated for a further period of one year – from October 19, 2026, to October 18, 2027 – or until a regular chairman is appointed, whichever is earlier.
Dr Abidi had initially been appointed as the PCSIR chairman on October 19, 2020, for a standard three-year term.

As per the standard practices, the ministry notifies committees for the scrutiny and selection of a suitable candidate for the post; however, no committee was notified following receipt of the applications, the sources alleged.

stories.title: Karachi sees sharp rise in ‘encounter’ killings as 200 shot dead in 10 months
summary: The data maintained by Karachi police shows that besides killing 197 suspects, police encounters left 1,426 others wounded — a 67.9pc rise from 849 arrested in wounded condition during the same period last year.
There was also a 71pc surge in the number of police encounters in 2026, compared to 840 in the corresponding period last year.

When contacted, two senior police officers, who wished not to be named, claimed that all killings of suspects in encounters were genuine as such actions were taken on main roads on complaints of robbery victims.

stories.title: BISE postpones papers in Jhelum over Punjab CM Maryam's visit
summary: RAWALPINDI: The Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (BISE) Rawalpindi has postponed the Computer Science papers of the Intermediate Second Annual Examinations 2026 scheduled for November 10 (Tuesday), fixing November 30 as the new date.
According to a letter addressed to the BISE Rawalpindi chairman, the deputy commissioner recommended postponing the computer science papers in Jhelum district.

He said the computer science papers of the Intermediate Second Annual Examination 2026, scheduled for Tuesday, November 10, had been postponed in Jhelum district following the recommendation of the deputy commissioner in view of administrative arrangements in the district.

He said the suspect was being taken to a place for recovery when at least three armed accomplices intercepted the police team and opened fire in an attempt to secure his release from custody.

stories.title: Three of the same family killed after high-voltage cable falls on house in Punjab's Bahawalnagar
summary: BAHAWALNAGAR: Three members of the same family were electrocuted to death when a high-voltage 11KVA transmission line above their house snapped and fell on them in Fort Abbas here on Saturday.
A report issued by Rescue 1122 stated that around 12:30am on Nov 7 an 11KVA electricity line passing over a house in Chak 272/HR snapped and fell on three individuals inside, killing them instantly.

When contacted, Mepco Bahawalnagar Superintending Engineer (SE) Khalid Sial claimed that no cable was broken or repaired and said that Multan-based investigation teams were on their way to the location to look into the matter.

stories.title: Balochistan, Punjab governors discuss ties
summary: The Balochistan governor emphasised the need to draw on Punjab’s experience and expertise to promote higher education in Balochistan, enhance the capacity of public-sector universities, encourage research activities and establish stronger links between educational institutions.

The Punjab governor assured him that students from Balochistan would be provided opportunities to gain admission to quality educational institutions in Punjab, along with all possible facilities and support to pursue higher education.

Governor Mandokhail also invited his Punjab counterpart to visit Quetta to explore further avenues of cooperation between the two provinces and make practical progress on educational and development-related initiatives.

stories.title: Smaller pie, firmer grip
summary: Technological and institutional changes can expand economic opportunities while simultaneously creating new centres of political power.
The political economy consideration here is that meaningful fiscal autonomy changes the distribution of power.
These three cases are not identical, but they share a key feature: an economically promising change can redistribute political power, creating incentives for incumbents to resist or dilute it.

stories.title: Trump’s choice
summary: ALTHOUGH American President Donald Trump has admitted that the disastrous Iran war was a factor in the heavy drubbing his party received from the Democrats in the midterm polls, there are few indications he has decided to wind down the conflict.
Qatar has taken centre stage in mediation, with Mr Trump discussing the Iran file with the country’s emir.
If Iran does retaliate to new American or Israeli strikes, the impact of the conflict could be far more devastating than the last round.

stories.title: Ruling coalition inches ahead on electoral reforms
summary: ISLAMABAD: The ruling coalition partners have formally submitted the names of their nominees for the proposed parliamentary committee on electoral reforms, while nominations from opposition parties are still awaited.

Interestingly, Dr Chaudhry said his own party, the ruling PML-N, had shortlisted names for the committee, but these would be submitted to the National Assembly Secretariat only after final approval from the party leadership.
Replying to a question, Dr Chaudhry said that if opposition parties decided to boycott the committee, the leadership of the ruling coalition parties would make a final decision on the matter.

stories.title: Ex-AJK president Raja Zulqarnain dies at 93
summary: Raja Zulqarnain entered politics in 1960-61 as an associate of KH Khurshid, former AJK president and private secretary to Quaid-i-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah.
Ahead of AJK’s first general elections under the parliamentary system in 1975, Raja Zulqarnain joined the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) and was elected to the Legislative Assembly from Samahni.

In his condolence message, AJK Legislative Assembly Speaker Chaudhry Tariq Farooq described Raja Zulqarnain’s death as a major loss for the political, parliamentary and social circles of Jammu and Kashmir.

stories.title: PHC removes pleas against emergency, detentions from cause lists
summary: The move comes a day after the high court’s administrative committee, acting in compliance with a restraining order issued by the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC), decided not to proceed with petitions filed under Article 199 of the Constitution on or after Oct 12.
Several petitions challenging detentions under the Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, which had also been fixed for Nov 10, were deleted from the cause list.

It termed the “limiting” of the fundamental rights of 45 million people in KP through a court order a serious blow to the supremacy of the Constitution, independence of the judiciary and the right to justice.

stories.title: SMOKERS’ CORNER: Bollywood’s Hold on Pakistan
summary: How do Pakistani audiences reconcile their appetite for Indian cinema with the hostile political narratives increasingly embedded in Bollywood films?
So how do Pakistani viewers cope with the dichotomy of putting anti-Pakistan Indian films at the top on streaming services?

Indian cultural products engage Pakistani audiences by treating them as cultural subordinates, moulding their mindset to mirror and reinforce India’s broader political and cultural hegemony in the region.

stories.title: Murree administration devises plan to facilitate winter tourists
summary: The meeting reviewed the ‘Snow season contingency plan’ and relevant departments were directed to complete all necessary preparations in advance.
Instructions were issued regarding the digital monitoring of vehicles entering Murree, inspection of vehicles arriving without anti-skid chains.
Later, the Lahore High Court Rawalpindi bench directed officials concerned to make winter plans to deal with traffic and other issues before the start of the winter season in the hill station.

stories.title: Over 100 structures demolished along Islamabad Expressway
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has sealed 58 buildings and demolished 124 structures between Sohan and Khanna Bridge along Islamabad Expressway Service Road (East), where development work on a major road-widening project is also underway.

Mr Ashraf said completion of the service road would help ease traffic congestion on the Islamabad Expressway, reduce commuters’ travel time and fuel consumption and improve travelling facilities for residents of adjoining areas.
The CDA claimed that work has been progressing simultaneously on all sections of the project.

The committee recommended that the State Bank of Pakistan and commercial banks establish a minimum 33 per cent benchmark for women’s participation in youth and agricultural loans.

stories.title: Woman alleges harassment by ex-husband on court premises
summary: LAHORE: A British Pakistani woman pursuing maintenance litigation against her former husband for their three daughters has alleged harassment and intimidation by him on the court’s premises.
In her application submitted to the Islampura police, the complainant, Laleen, alleged that she had visited the sessions court for a hearing against her ex-husband, a businessman.

LHC dismisses plea challenging guardian court’s decision on maintenance allowance for three daughters According to the complaint filed on Oct 23, the former husband repeatedly demanded custody of their daughters, issued death threats, and physically shoved her.

stories.title: Sindh CM declares Tharparkar drought-hit, orders relief measures
summary: KARACHI: Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah on Saturday declared Tharparkar a drought-affected district after reviewing the situation and the severe crop losses.
He directed the relevant departments to begin relief work immediately and to ensure that drinking water and essential supplies were available to the affected population.
Presiding over a meeting at the CM House, Mr Shah was briefed on drought-like conditions in all seven talukas of the district.

stories.title: Remand of nine suspects extended in credit card data theft case
summary: KARACHI: A court on Saturday allowed the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) to keep the custody of nine suspects arrested during a raid on a call centre in connection with the credit card data theft case for further questioning till Nov 10.
The judicial magistrate (East) also reserved his order on the bail applications of detained suspects, including the owner of the call centre for the next hearing.
The counsel for the suspects opposed further physical remand and also filed post-arrest bail applications and argued that recoveries have already been made and their custody was no more required.

stories.title: Registration of traders seeking tax relief goes online in GB
summary: GILGIT: Gilgit-Baltistan Chief Minister Amjad Hussain on Saturday inaugurated an online registration system for traders seeking tax exemption on goods imported from China through the Khunjerab Pass for local consumption in the region.
Speaking at the ceremony, the chief minister said GB traders would benefit from the tax exemption facility granted by the federal government for Pakistan-China trade through the Khunjerab Pass.

CM says govt to establish trade-free zone in Gilgit using its own resources He said the tax exemption scheme aimed to facilitate local traders and residents while promoting economic activity in the region.

stories.title: IHC declares badminton federation elections illegal
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has declared the Pakistan Badminton Federation’s (PBF) elections held on Oct 24, 2025, illegal and directed the Pakistan Sports Board (PSB) to conduct fresh elections within 90 days.

The IHC also directed the formation of an ad hoc committee, hea­ded by the Additional Secr­e­tary of the Ministry of Inter-Pro­vincial Coordination, to over­­see the federation’s affairs until the completion of the election process.
The ad hoc committee will be responsible for managing the day-to-day affairs of the federation until the newly elected body of the Pakis­tan Badminton Federation formally assumes charge.

stories.title: Tents flooded as heavy rain hits Gaza
summary: GAZA CITY: Heavy rain on Saturday flooded tens of thousands of displaced people’s tents in the war-devastated Gaza, Palestinian authorities said, leaving many of them without shelter.
About “70,000 tents sheltering tens of thousands of displaced people were flooded on the first day” of rains, the Hamas-run government media office stated.
The coalition, which includes dozens of local institutions and organisations, called for “pressure on Israel to allow the entry of humanitarian aid without restrictions”.

stories.title: Tongue out of Australia white-ball tour
summary: England fast bowler Josh Tongue has been ruled out of their white-ball tour of Australia with a toe injury and will return home for treatment, the team said Sunday.
Tongue arrived in Perth last week ahead of England's three-match ODI and five-game T20 series, but sat out their 92-run one-day warm-up win over Western Australia on Saturday.
"Josh Tongue has been ruled out of the white-ball tour of Australia due to a left big toe injury," team officials said.

stories.title: Loud booms heard in Saudi capital Riyadh after early warning alert issued
summary: Multiple loud booms were heard in the Saudi capital, Riyadh, shortly after Civil Defence issued an early-warning alert of a potential threat on Sunday, a Reuters witness said, as hostilities between the kingdom and Yemen's Houthis persisted.

Saudi Civil Defence later said the danger had passed. on early Sunday, Saudi Arabia's air defence systems intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched toward the eastern region, a spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition announced.
Gen. Turki al-Maliki said in a statement that Yemen's Houthi group targeted Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province with the missile.

stories.title: UAE says it rescued 22 people after cargo ship caught fire in Sea of Oman
summary: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards say 2 oil tankers hit mines, caught fire near Strait of Hormuz Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said on late Saturday that two oil tankers were burning after striking naval mines in and near the Strait of Hormuz.
CENTCOM further said US forces had destroyed 10 Iranian commercial oil tankers allegedly linked to a multibillion-dollar shadow network operated by Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps.
